correctness.rationale: Exact wheel grounding gives A=3I-S-S^T; its periodized positive Green kernel c_d and squared kernel u_d are derived by solving the second-order recurrence. Rank-two pseudoinverse updating yields direct damage and interaction identities with positive denominators, and exact 222 wheel computations agree. Discrete convexity makes c_d,u_d and Y_d strictly decreasing, implying the unique adjacent maximum and single interaction sign transition. Exact Y at n=3,...,7 plus an all-n geometric tail bound (strictly below 1 from n=8 onward) prove the sharp onset at six rim vertices. The asymptotic threshold follows by uniform periodization estimates at d=O(log n); finite data are not used as infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a motivated network-failure optimization: a wheel is the canonical hub-and-ring redundancy architecture, and total effective resistance quantifies network-wide degradation. The theorem gives the exact worst pair, proves that failure synergy becomes antagonistic only from the sharp n=6 threshold, and localizes the crossover separation at a nonobvious logarithmic-plus-logarithmic scale. These are structural and asymptotic distinctions beyond routine substitution into existing Green functions, and may guide robust spoke placement and failure aggregation assessments.
